author: Henry Ketcham
claims: The election occurred on the sixth day of November.
Abraham Lincoln received one hundred and eighty electoral votes.
The electoral vote was officially announced in a joint session of Congress on February 13, 1861.
Abraham Lincoln was officially elected President of the United States for a four-year term beginning March 4, 1861.
There was concern among party members about the Baltimore revelations.
Many men of local influence met Lincoln during the Peace Conference.
J. G. Holland estimated that not more than one in five people in Washington in the winter of 1860-61 were glad to have Lincoln come.
There was a scheme to foment discontent and division throughout the North on the eve of the presidential election.
